sources.entry: Mactokio - Native TOTP/HOTP authenticator that imports accounts by webcam QR scan and keeps secrets AES-256 encrypted on device. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/dalirnet/mactokio) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Mactokio is a native macOS TOTP/HOTP authenticator app that imports accounts by scanning a QR code with the Mac's webcam and keeps secrets AES-256 encrypted on the device.
summary.what_it_does: Generates TOTP and HOTP one-time codes using SHA-1, SHA-256, or SHA-512. Accounts can be added by scanning a QR code with the webcam (confidence-based detection across frames), by loading a QR image or text file, or by pasting a QR screenshot or otpauth:// URI from the clipboard. It accepts standard otpauth:// URIs and Google Authenticator bulk migration (otpauth-migration://) links. Secrets are encrypted with AES-256 using a key derived by SHA-256 from the device hardware UUID, stored in files with 700/600 POSIX permissions, and protected by Touch ID or device password on each launch. The app states it has no network access, no sync, no cloud, and no telemetry. It also offers search and filtering, one-tap copy, and auto-locking of codes after 3 cycles.
use_cases: Replace a phone authenticator app with codes on a Mac
Import 2FA accounts from a phone without exporting a QR screenshot
Move Google Authenticator accounts to a Mac
Generate TOTP or HOTP one-time codes for logins
Store two-factor secrets locally without a cloud account
how_to_run: Extract and move Mactokio.app to Applications
Right-click the app and choose Open the first time to bypass Gatekeeper
Build from source: make build (build the app) or make run (build and launch)
make release builds a universal binary (arm64 + x86_64)
make dist builds the release and zips it for distribution
notable: Webcam QR import so secrets never pass through screenshots, email, or chat
Google Authenticator bulk migration imports many accounts in one scan
Secrets encrypted with a key derived from the device hardware UUID
Zero network access with no cloud, sync, or account
Universal binary build for Apple silicon and Intel
caveats: First launch needs right-click Open to bypass Gatekeeper, since the app is distributed unsigned via Releases as the README implies
Secrets are tied to the device hardware, so the README does not describe moving them to another Mac
